name: Bolandiol

lead: Bolandiol is a nandrolone-like anabolic steroid. Its dipropionate ester has been marketed in the past, but the base compound never was.
In castrated rats it raised lean mass and bone density. Wikipedia reports clinical studies found no change in strength, body composition or performance.

paras: It binds the androgen receptor weakly but also has estrogenic and progestational activity, and it suppresses gonadotropins and endogenous testosterone.
It suppresses natural testosterone production in animals. It is on the WADA prohibited list.

lead: Bolandiol (19-nor-4-androstenediol, estr-4-ene-3beta,17beta-diol) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid related to nandrolone. The base compound was never marketed, though its dipropionate ester (anabiol) has been sold.[1] The World Anti-Doping Agency lists it as prohibited.[1]

Animal research describes it as unusual among anabolic steroids because it has androgenic, estrogenic and progestational activity. In castrated adult male rats it increased lean mass and bone mineral density without strongly stimulating sex accessory glands.[2] Wikipedia states that several clinical studies concluded it did not change strength, body composition or exercise performance, although the source studies are not in the cited literature reviewed here.[1]

paras: A 2010 study found bolandiol bound the androgen receptor with lower affinity than testosterone or nandrolone, yet suppressed gonadotropins and endogenous testosterone production, and had estrogenic and progestational effects in addition to androgenic ones.[2] It may be metabolised to nandrolone or a related compound.[1] Earlier rat work compared its effect on prostate androgen receptor levels with those of androgens and other anabolic steroids.[3]

Bolandiol has been used as a comparison compound in animal models for evaluating selective androgen receptor modulators.[4] A guinea pig MRI study examined anabolic steroid precursors and growth effects on skeletal muscle.[5] A 1981 rat study of bolandiol dipropionate examined its effect on chemically induced liver cancer development.[6]
No studies found in the reviewed literature beyond preclinical work; Wikipedia summarises older clinical studies as showing no change in strength, body composition or performance.[1]
